method_note: Chose claims by impact on a conformance engine: (1) every Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 article and letter cited in conformance_implications, re-read in the consolidated text (publications.europa.eu cellar, chunks at offsets 300000 to 500000); (2) existing_check and new_capability claims, compared with docs/reference/capabilities.md and architecture.md section on identifier.parse; (3) DOI, title, year, venue and first author for 24 papers at Crossref or OpenAlex; (4) key_contribution and classification_scheme claims against OpenAlex abstracts and, where the file says full text was read, against the open PDFs (Shamsir, Wiesner, Nowacki, Garcia, Trienens). Crossref returned no abstract for most records, so abstract-level claims were checked at OpenAlex. Papers whose abstracts are not retrievable are marked not_confirmed, not refuted.

checked.claim: Art. 9(2)(d) and Art. 10(1)(f): the product-group act decides model, batch or item level.
checked.evidence: Art. 9(2)(d) lists model, batch or item level as a delegated-act item; Art. 10(1)(f) requires data to refer to the level the delegated act sets.

checked.claim: Art. 10(1)(a) persistent unique identifier via data carrier; Art. 10(4) back-up copy at a service provider; Art. 11(e) availability also after insolvency, liquidation or cessation.
checked.evidence: 10(1)(a), 10(4) and 11(e) read as described. Note 11(e) says 'stops operating in the EU' as well as insolvency and liquidation.

checked.claim: Art. 10(1)(d) open standards, machine-readable, no vendor lock-in; Art. 11(a) interoperability on technical, semantic, organisational aspects; Art. 11(c) storage by operator or service provider.
Art. 10(1)(d) machine-readable, structured, searchable; Art. 9(2)(a) with Annex III.
checked.evidence: 9(2)(a) names the data per Annex III; 10(1)(d) names machine-readable and searchable.

checked.claim: Art. 9(2)(f) who accesses which data; 10(1)(g) and 11(b) access by named actor groups; 11(f) update rights limited by access rights.
checked.evidence: All four letters match.

checked.claim: Art. 11(g) authentication, reliability, integrity; Art. 11(h) security, privacy, fraud avoided.
checked.evidence: 11(g) and 11(h) match. The Garcia paper quotes the same letters.

checked.claim: Art. 9(1) data accurate, complete, up to date; Art. 9(2)(g) and (h) who may create or update and the update process; Art. 11(d) link to the original passport.
checked.evidence: 9(1) requires correct, thorough, current data; 9(2)(g) actors who create or update; 9(2)(h) detailed entry/update process; 11(d) new passport linked to earlier ones.

checked.claim: The paper cites Art. 9(2)(h) for availability; the consolidated text puts availability in 9(2)(i), and (h) is the update process.
checked.evidence: The PDF text (R-04) derives availability from Art. 9.2.(h). The regulation text lists availability duration under 9(2)(i) and the entry/update process under (h). The file's correction is right.

checked.claim: Nine requirements R-01 to R-09 with the stated topics; R-02 granularity from Art. 9.2.(d), R-05 from 9.2.(g), R-06 from 9.2.(f), R-07 and R-08 from 11(g)/(h).
checked.evidence: R-01 to R-09 topics match. R-09 derives from Art. 5.11 and 5.5 of the regulation, which the file does not name (minor). R-01 in the paper points to a protected ISO/IEC identifier standard; the file correctly omits it.

checked.claim: Taxonomy by the Nickerson method, 32 papers, 50 cases, three iterations, 21 dimensions in four meta-dimensions, two experts; venue INFORMATIK 2025 LNI.
checked.evidence: GI page: INFORMATIK 2025, NaWerSys workshop, Potsdam, LNI P366, 32 papers and 50 use cases. PDF text: Nickerson method, three iterations, '21 dimensions ... four meta-dimensions', two DPP experts. Author order Shamsir, Paeplow, Moller confirmed. The AI search engine was Perplexity.ai used as an alternative search engine; file wording is acceptable.

checked.claim: Reference architecture with five layers plus two axes; communication level has seven layers; compliance engine is a back-end component.
checked.evidence: Page lists five levels (data, communication, architecture, function, potential), axes life cycle and hierarchy, a seven-layer communication level, and the compliance engine as a back-end service. OpenAlex: Proc. Design Society vol. 6, 2026, CC BY-NC-ND. The OpenAlex abstract names four layers; the fifth (potential) is on the page.

checked.claim: Wiesner et al.: four capability layers data acquisition, data exchange, data processing, data access; 7-person expert panel with Likert survey; REST/JSON-LD, AAS, microservices, event-driven, RBAC; Python and SQL proof of concept.
checked.evidence: PDF: panel of 7 experts, five-point Likert scale, REST with JSON-LD payload, AAS-based models, microservices, event-driven, RBAC, Python programs with SQL databases. The first layer is named 'data collection' in the paper, not 'data acquisition'.
checked.correction: Rename the first capability layer to data collection.

checked.claim: Nowacki et al.: IOTA DAG ledger, nine design goals, smart-contract versioning.
checked.evidence: PDF text names IOTA, IOTA Smart Contracts, a DAG-based ledger, and design goals such as controllable and extensible. The OpenAlex abstract does not name IOTA, so only the full text supports it.

checked.claim: 225 studies, more than twenty attributes, blockchain most proposed, hybrid architectures.
checked.evidence: Title, year 2026, venue and abstract figures match. Crossref and OpenAlex list two authors (Psarommatis, May). OpenAlex says CC BY-NC-ND hybrid open access; the file's OA URL is correct.

checked.claim: Lyse et al.: two-axis scheme, archetypes data-centric, layered, technology-anchored, ecosystem-oriented, validation gaps.
checked.evidence: Title, year 2026, venue Digital, first author match. Abstract lists data-centric, layered and ecosystem-oriented structures and validation by case study, stakeholder assessment or prototype. 'Technology-anchored' and the 'two axes' wording were not visible in the retrieved abstract.

checked.claim: Wan: 25 frameworks, four review areas, QR and RFID carriers, blockchain security, third-party update gap.
checked.evidence: All figures match. Co-author Shanshan Jiang exists. Volume 54, pp. 362-374.

checked.claim: Kaser et al.: three dimensions (data carrier, online storage, updating dynamic data); cross-cutting counterfeiting, interoperability, data sovereignty; not open access.
checked.evidence: OpenAlex abstract matches, is_oa false, authors Kaser, Lesjak, Matischek, Steger. Crossref confirms CNSM 2025, issued 27 Oct 2025.

checked.claim: Gering et al. 2024: three service classes (central, DPP system, third party); six authors.
checked.evidence: Title, year 2024, Fraunhofer-Publica conference paper, abstract and author list match. OpenAlex also lists a bogus ':unav' author entry.

checked.claim: Gering: test environment position paper; modular tests; emulation of central components; open access.
checked.evidence: Authors Gering, Knothe, Schulz (Fraunhofer IPK). Abstract matches; CC BY diamond OA. Abstract calls the aim a freely accessible test environment; 'position paper' is the file's own label.
checked.correction: The file lists only the first author; add Knothe and Schulz.

checked.claim: JRC method: essential, strongly recommended, voluntary tiers; system design only for access rights, governance, granularity.
checked.evidence: Abstract matches. The record does not define the tiers or criteria, so the conformance use (fail for essential, warn for others) is the file's own proposal. The method uses a value-effort assessment.

checked.claim: First author is 'Paula Hess' with the sharp-s; Crossref spells Hess and Consensus spells Heess.
checked.evidence: Crossref metadata spells the family name with double e plus sharp s (Heess form). The file reverses the two spellings and records the name wrongly in first_author. Four requirements listed in the abstract match.
checked.correction: Set first_author to Paula Heeß and state that Crossref uses Heeß.

checked.claim: King et al.: nine high-level capabilities; issue year 2023.
checked.evidence: Title, journal, first author, print year 2023 (vol. 384) confirmed. Crossref has no abstract, so 'nine capabilities' could not be verified.

checked.claim: Kranner et al.: layered blueprint of data space, AAS, CIRPASS semantic models, GS1 identification and event semantics.
checked.evidence: Abstract matches (data space governance, AAS, CIRPASS data models plus shared vocabularies, GS1). Procedia CS vol. 277, CC BY. The file's 'CIRPASS semantic models for shared vocabularies' merges two items; minor.

checked.claim: Boero: SHACL workbench, Python package and container MCP server, BatteryPass v1.2.0 comparison with 14 strict overlap pairs; ORE article 6-234.
checked.evidence: Abstract matches, including 14 strict overlap pairs and the 19-module recommendation. A second author, Miguel Las Heras Hernandez, exists.

checked.claim: Samarathunga: layered architecture, SHACL validation, explanation model, analysis of two CIRPASS datasets, five dimensions.
checked.evidence: Title, 2026, venue and first author match. OpenAlex has no abstract; the SHACL, CIRPASS and five-dimension claims rest on the Consensus excerpt only. Co-authors Horsch and Al Machot (NMBU) exist.

checked.claim: Abreu: two-year design science, textile prototype, eleven design principles.
checked.evidence: All three facts in the abstract. Published online Feb 2025, IJPR vol. 63 issue 16.

checked.claim: Khairy: 16 experiments, single host, 100 percent EPCIS 2.0 compliance, Groth16, IOTA.
checked.evidence: Crossref abstract states 16 experiments, single-host testbed, 100% EPCIS 2.0 compliance, Groth16 and IOTA.

checked.claim: identifier.parse accepts only /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>; batch (lot) and model forms are refused.
checked.evidence: Architecture text: one GS1 Digital Link form; forms GS1 permits, such as a GTIN without serial, a key qualifier, or a path prefix, give IDENTIFIER.SYNTAX.INVALID. The file's listed extensions (GTIN only, lot qualifiers, path prefix) match.

checked.claim: carrier.nfc, carrier.rfid, api.fuzz, data.shacl, integrity.cose, integrity.status_list, persistence.scheduled, registry.official, evidence.untp_dcc are interface_only; aas.validate and persistence.versions are experimental; registry.mock is supported.
checked.evidence: Manifest rows match. Check name carrier.qr_decode maps to capability carrier.qr; access.restricted_fields maps to access.policy; registry.consistency maps to registry.mock. The file uses check names and capability names interchangeably but correctly.

checked.claim: Status list checking is missing (integrity.status_list is interface_only), so VC status needs new work.
checked.evidence: integrity.status_list is interface_only, but the manifest also lists evidence.status_list as supported: it verifies an operator-supplied signed Bitstring Status List file. The file never mentions it, so 'missing' overstates the gap for offline status files.
checked.correction: State that evidence.status_list (supported) verifies a supplied status list file; only passport-side status retrieval (integrity.status_list) is interface_only.

checked.claim: Item-level GS1 forms are parseable today; batch forms are not.
checked.evidence: Only /01/GTIN/21/serial is accepted; a lot qualifier gives IDENTIFIER.SYNTAX.INVALID.

checked.claim: Title, year, venue and first author for Jansen, Havur, Ebel, Belova, Robal.
checked.evidence: Crossref returned the same title, year, container and first author for all five. Only Jansen has a retrievable abstract (matches). The other four have no abstract at Crossref, so their key_contribution text is unverified.

checked.claim: Title, year, venue and first author for Petrik (two), Tzionis, Abdallah, Fabianek, Malo.
checked.evidence: All six match. Petrik's Electronic Markets paper has 6 authors. Abstract claims were not checkable at Crossref.

rule5_findings.problem: The entry says the search snippets summarized a draft CEN standard 'on storage and persistence'. This reveals the subject scope of a protected draft and comes from a secondary source.
rule5_findings.fix: Reword to: search snippets about a CEN draft were seen and not read; nothing from them is recorded.

rule5_findings.problem: Mentions that the paper lists standard numbers from Annex III. Naming is allowed, but the paper's R-01 ties product identifiers to a protected ISO/IEC identifier standard; the file's R-01 summary says only 'ISO identifier'. This is acceptable as a name, so this is a low-severity watch item.
rule5_findings.fix: Keep the bare name only; add no description of what that standard requires.

missed_items.fact: The capability manifest lists evidence.status_list as supported (offline verification of an operator-supplied signed status list), separate from integrity.status_list (interface_only). CI-08 and the Abdallah entry should mention both.

The Gering et al. abstract says the EU Battery Regulation makes passports mandatory for certain batteries from 2027. The file does not state this date; it should cite Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 and re-check the article before use.

Art. 10(1)(c) ties the carrier and identifier to listed standards or equivalents until harmonised standards exist. The file's CI-01 and CI-02 could cite it as the legal route to the protected carrier standards without describing them.

Art. 9(2)(e) requires delegated acts to say how customers see the passport before purchase, including online sales. No conformance implication covers it; it could map to identifier.resolve on a public channel.

overall: The file is largely reliable. All 8 legal citations to Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 matched the consolidated text letter by letter, and the correction of the Garcia et al. citation slip is right. Bibliographic data (titles, years, venues, first authors) matched for 30 papers. One factual error was found (the Heeß spelling is reversed, and the first-author field is wrong), one minor layer-name slip (Wiesner), and a few missing co-authors. The weakest area is abstract-level content for papers where only Consensus text was available (for example Samarathunga, King, Havur, Ebel): the file honestly marks them metadata_only, but those claims could not be re-verified. Engine mappings are correct except that the status-list gap ignores the supported evidence.status_list capability. Rule 5 risk is low; one anomaly line should be reworded.
